widgets_values:
Exercise: train a shape classifier on ComfyUI-synthesized data (HOG + SVM)

ComfyUI as a synthetic-data factory: nothing is loaded or downloaded. Three shape classes (circle / square / triangle) are drawn on a blank canvas with raw cv2 primitives, then AUGMENTED into 12 tiles each - rotations via cv2.getRotationMatrix2D + cv2.warpAffine, sensor noise via the 'Add Gaussian noise (gray)' subgraph, a brightness/contrast shift via cv2.convertScaleAbs - exactly the nuisance variation a real classifier must shrug off.

'CV HOG Features' reduces every tile to the 81-dim gradient-orientation descriptor of OpenCV's digits.py tutorial (win 20, cell 10, 9 bins): edges and corners survive, absolute brightness mostly cancels. 'CV Stack Feature Classes' labels the rows, and 'CV Train Classifier' (SVM, RBF, trainAuto cross-validation) fits on a per-class train split and scores the HELD-OUT tiles: the test accuracy readout and the confusion matrix heatmap (row = true class, col = predicted; a clean run lights only the diagonal). Chance is 0.33 - the margin above it is what the descriptor + model actually learned. The model itself never leaves the node (cache safety); model_yaml exposes it for reuse outside ComfyUI.

SAVED FOR REUSE: 'CV Save Classifier' writes the trained SVM to ComfyUI/models/cvml/shape_classifier_hog.yml.gz (gzip-compressed OpenCV YAML). Run THIS workflow once, then open exercise_classifier_reuse.json - it loads the file with 'CV Predict Classifier' and classifies a FRESH set of shape tiles without retraining.

FAILURE PATH (bottom): stacking one real class with an empty one leaves a single-class training set - the trainer answers success=false with safe empty outputs instead of raising.
